notes.en: Formulas are the bread and butter of Excel. They allow you to perform calculations on your data. Every formula begins with an equals sign (=). For example, =SUM(A1:A10) adds up all the values in cells A1 through A10.
notes.rw: Imiterere y'imibare (formulas) ni ingenzi cyane muri Excel. Ikubashisha gukora imibare ku makuru yawe. Buri miterere yose itangirwa n'ikimenyetso cya kunganya (=). Kurugero, =SUM(A1:A10) iteranya agaciro kose kari mu tuzu (cells) kuva kuri A1 kugeza kuri A10.

notes.en: Formatting makes your data easier to read and understand. You can change fonts, colors, and borders. Conditional formatting is a powerful tool that changes the appearance of cells based on specific conditions. Charts and graphs help visualize data trends.
notes.rw: Gutunganya (formatting) bituma amakuru yawe asomeka kandi akumvikana neza. Ushobora guhindura inyuguti, amabara, n'imipaka (borders). 'Conditional formatting' ni igikoresho gikomeye gihindura uko utuzu (cells) tugaragara bitewe n'imiterere yihariye. Imbonerahamwe (charts/graphs) zifasha kureba uko amakuru ahinduka.
